Prealgebra · Lesson 4.7

Mixed Numbers

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Seven quarter-hops carry you across a creek from 00. After 44 hops your boot lands on 11, and three more put you past 11 but short of 22. You can call that spot seven quarters, 7447​, or one whole plank and three quarters more, 134143​. Same point, two names. The second name is a mixed number, and this lesson is about writing them and converting between the two forms.

Problem
Your boot is at 7447​, past 11 but short of 22. How many whole planks have you completely crossed? Give that count.
Show a hint
  • A whole plank only counts as finished if your boot is fully past its far end. You sailed past the mark at 11, but you stopped before reaching the mark at 22, so the second plank is only partly crossed. How many planks did you finish all the way?
  • Count up the quarter-hops. Four quarter-hops carry you across one whole plank to the mark at 11. You took seven hops, which is four to reach 11 and three more past it. Those three extra hops have not yet reached 22, so only the planks behind the mark at 11 are truly finished.
Show the full solution
Four quarter-hops make one whole plank, so the marks land at 00, 44=144​=1, and 84=248​=2. Seven hops puts your boot at 7447​, past the mark at 11 but short of 22, so you have finished 11​ plank. Those three extra quarter-hops are the 3443​ in the mixed number 134143​.
Problem
Order slip: 327372​ bands. Three whole bands = 2121 beads, then add 22 loose. Write 327372​ as an improper fraction in sevenths.
Show a hint
  • A whole band is not really one thing to the machine, it is 7 beads. So how many single beads hide inside the 3 whole bands before you even touch the loose ones?
  • Three whole bands are 3×7=213×7=21 beads. Add the 2 loose beads to get the total bead count, then write that total over 7, since each bead is one seventh of a band.
Show the full solution
Each whole band is 7 beads, so 3 bands hold 3×7=213×7=21 beads. Add the 2 loose beads for 2323 beads in all, and every bead is one seventh of a band. 327=3×7+27=237372​=73×7+2​=723​​ Going backwards, 23÷723÷7 is 3 with remainder 2, which lands on 327372​ again.
Problem
A lookout sits at 476647​ miles. Convert to a mixed number. Give the nearest post behind the hiker, the largest whole number below 476647​.
Show a hint
  • A mixed number is really a division. How many whole groups of 66 fit inside 4747, and how much is left over? That whole count is the milepost she has already passed.
  • Divide 4747 by 66. It goes in 77 times because 6×7=426×7=42, with 55 left over, so 476=756647​=765​. The 77 is the whole part, so the lookout sits past post 77 but not yet at post 88.
Show the full solution
Each whole mile is 6666​, so ask how many 66's fit into 4747. Since 6×7=426×7=42 with 55 left over, 476=756647​=765​. She is past post 77 and not yet at post 88, so the post behind her is 77​. The whole part of a mixed number is always the largest whole number below it.
Problem
A stretch is 2323 beads, and every 55 beads make one full band (235523​). Divide 2323 by 55: whole bands and leftover. Write the length as a mixed number.
Show a hint
  • The bottom number 5 is your group size, so you are really asking how many full fives fit inside 23. Count up in fives, 5, 10, 15, 20, and notice how far you can go before passing 23.
  • Divide 23 by 5. The quotient is the number of whole bands, and the remainder is the loose beads left over, which sit on top of 5 in the fraction part.
Show the full solution
23÷523÷5 gives 44 with a remainder of 33, since 5×4=205×4=20 and 23−20=323−20=3. So 23 beads make 4 complete bands with 3 loose beads, and those 3 beads are 3553​ of a band. 235=435523​=453​​ The quotient becomes the whole part and the remainder sits over the same bottom number.
Key idea
A mixed number like 134143​ means 1+341+43​. It names the whole part first and only the leftover, so it marks the same point as the improper fraction 7447​. To turn an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide, since the fraction bar means division. Dividing 2323 by 55 gives a quotient of 44 and a remainder of 33. The quotient is the whole part and the remainder stays over the same denominator. To go back, split each whole into as many pieces as the denominator and count them all, which is whole×bottom+topwhole×bottom+top. Neither direction changes the size of a piece, so neither changes the number.
Fun fact
In 756765​ the space means "and" (++), a surveyors' shorthand. Once algebra arrives, juxtaposition means multiply (2x2x), so mixed-number notation is quietly retired.
Problem
Sensor at −713−731​: the minus covers the whole quantity, so the sensor is a third below −7−7. Give −713−731​ as an improper fraction.
Show a hint
  • First locate where 7 1/3 lives on the positive side. It sits a third of the way past 7, between 7 and 8. Now reflect that whole spot across 0. Reflecting flips left and right, so whatever was just past 7 going up lands just past -7 going down.
  • The minus out front belongs to the entire amount, so -7 1/3 means -(7 1/3) = -(7 + 1/3) = -7 - 1/3. That is a third below -7, landing between -8 and -7. To get the improper fraction, write 7 1/3 = (7 times 3 + 1)/3 = 22/3, then attach the minus.
Show the full solution
The minus covers the whole amount, so −713=−(7+13)−731​=−(7+31​). Convert the positive part, 713=7×3+13=223731​=37×3+1​=322​, then attach the minus. −713=−223−731​=−322​​ The second sign flips too, so the sensor sits a third below −7−7, between −8−8 and −7−7, not a third above it.
Key idea
A minus sign in front of a mixed number applies to the whole quantity, not just the whole part. So −713−731​ means −7−13−7−31​, which is one third below −7−7 and between −8−8 and −7−7. The safe move is to put the minus sign on a single improper fraction, or to find the positive 713731​ and mirror that distance across 00. That keeps −713−731​ separate from −7+13−7+31​, a different number between −7−7 and −6−6.
Problem
Potter uses 256+156265​+165​ scoops. The fraction parts sum past 11, so carry a whole. Total scoops as a mixed number?
Show a hint
  • Keep the two columns apart for a moment. The whole scoops add to 2+1=32+1=3. Now add the sixths on their own, 56+5665​+65​. That fraction sum is going to be bigger than 11, which is the whole point of this problem.
  • 56+56=10665​+65​=610​, and 106610​ is one whole scoop plus 4664​ left over, which simplifies to 123132​. Hand that extra whole scoop up to the whole count. You started with 33 wholes, the carry makes it 44, and 2332​ of a scoop stays behind.
Show the full solution
The wholes give 2+1=32+1=3 and the sixths give 56+56=10665​+65​=610​. Since 106=66+46=146=123610​=66​+64​=164​=132​, one whole scoop moves over to the whole count, making 3+1=43+1=4 with 2332​ left behind. 423 scoops432​ scoops​ That move is carrying, the same as carrying a ten in column addition, except here a full 6666​ is what carries.
Problem
Rail is 514541​ spans. Cut 234243​. Since 14<3441​<43​, trade one whole for 44 quarters. Finish and give what remains as a mixed number.
Show a hint
  • The trade does not change how much rail there is, it just changes how it is written. One whole span is the same as 4444​, so trading a whole into quarters turns 55 wholes and 1441​ into 44 wholes and a bigger pile of quarters. How many quarters are in that pile now?
  • After the trade you are looking at 454445​ minus 234243​. Subtract the quarters first, 54−3445​−43​, then subtract the wholes, 4−24−2. Put the two results together and simplify the fraction.
Show the full solution
One whole span is 4444​, so trade a whole out of the 55 and 514541​ becomes 454445​, the same length written differently. Now the columns subtract, 54−34=2445​−43​=42​ and 4−2=24−2=2, leaving 224242​. Halving top and bottom, 224=212242​=221​​ spans. Borrowing is carrying run backwards, one whole broken into denominator-many pieces.
Problem
Legs: 112+213121​+231​ laps. Halves and thirds differ, so find lcd, rename fractions, then add. Check for carry. Total as a mixed number?
Show a hint
  • Split each amount into its whole part and its fraction part. The wholes are 11 and 22, so those give 33 laps right away. The fractions 1221​ and 1331​ cannot be added as they stand because the pieces are different sizes, so first find a denominator that both 22 and 33 divide into.
  • Use 66 as the shared bottom. Rename 12=3621​=63​ and 13=2631​=62​, then add to get 36+26=5663​+62​=65​. Since 5665​ is less than one whole lap, there is nothing to carry, so just attach it to the 33 whole laps.
Show the full solution
The wholes give 1+2=31+2=3 laps. The fractions need a shared bottom, and 66 is the smallest number both 22 and 33 divide into, so 12=3621​=63​ and 13=2631​=62​, which add to 5665​. That is under one whole lap, so nothing carries, and the total is 356365​​ laps. As a single improper fraction that is 236623​, a quick way to check the work.
Key idea
Once the fraction parts share a denominator, adding or subtracting mixed numbers takes two steps. Combine wholes with wholes and fraction parts with fraction parts. If the fraction parts add past one whole, move that extra whole into the whole count and keep only the leftover fraction, so 256+356265​+365​ gives 55 and 5335​, which is 623632​. If you need to subtract more fraction than you have, rewrite one whole using that denominator, so with fourths one whole becomes 4444​. The first move is called carrying and the second is called borrowing.
Problem
44 planters each need 258285​ bags. Convert to an improper fraction, multiply by 44, convert back. Total bags as a mixed number?
Show a hint
  • Rewrite 258285​ as a single improper fraction before you touch the 44. Eighths times eighths stays in eighths, so the multiply step is clean.
  • 258=218285​=821​. Now 4×218=8484×821​=884​. Simplify that fraction, then split it into a whole number and a remaining fraction.
Show the full solution
258=168+58=218285​=816​+85​=821​, so 4×218=848=212.4×821​=884​=221​. Half of 2121 is 1010 with 11 left over, so the four boxes hold 10121021​​ bags. Keeping the parts separate is what causes slips here, since 4×58=2084×85​=820​ is itself more than two whole bags.
Problem
Full day: 334343​ km, and a half-staffed day gets 2332​ of that. Convert, multiply by 2332​, convert back. How many km, as a mixed number?
Show a hint
  • You cannot reliably take 2332​ of 33 and 2332​ of 3443​ separately and trust it. Turn 334343​ into a single improper fraction first. Three wholes is 124412​, so 334=154343​=415​. Now you just owe yourself 2332​ of 154415​.
  • Multiply straight across, top times top and bottom times bottom: 23×154=2×153×4=301232​×415​=3×42×15​=1230​. Now reduce 30121230​ by its biggest common factor, then split that improper fraction into a whole number and a leftover fraction.
Show the full solution
334=124+34=154343​=412​+43​=415​, so take 2332​ of it by multiplying straight across, 23×154=3012=5232​×415​=1230​=25​. Five halves is two wholes and one half, so the half-staffed day clears 212221​​ kilometres. The multiply rule only works on a plain fraction, so clear the mixed form first and fold it back at the end.
Key idea
Multiplying mixed numbers does not split into parts the way adding does. Each part of one number multiplies every part of the other, so multiplying the wholes and the fractions separately gives the wrong answer. Instead, rewrite each mixed number as a single improper fraction, then multiply numerators and denominators straight across. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction. Convert the result back to a mixed number at the end if the question asks for that form.
Problem
Ribbon 412421​ m, and bows are 3443​ m each. Convert, divide using flip-and-multiply. How many whole bows?
Show a hint
  • Before you can divide, the mixed number has to become a single fraction. Four and a half metres is the same as 9229​ metres, since two halves make each metre and there are nine halves in all. Now you are dividing 9229​ by 3443​.
  • Dividing by 3443​ means multiplying by its flip, 4334​. So compute 92×4329​×34​. Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms, then simplify and read off the whole number of pieces.
Show the full solution
412=92421​=29​, since each whole metre is two halves. Dividing by 3443​ is the same as multiplying by 4334​, so 92÷34=92×43=366=6.29​÷43​=29​×34​=636​=6​. The count comes out whole, so the ribbon splits into six 3443​-metre bows with nothing left over. Checking the other way, 6×34=184=4126×43​=418​=421​ metres.
Problem
A sign maker uses 158185​ m of ribbon per letter for a 44-letter word, starting from a 77 m roll. Convert, multiply, subtract. How many metres of ribbon are left on the roll?
Show a hint
  • Turn 158185​ into eighths first, since every letter uses the same amount. Four equal letters means you can multiply that single fraction by 44 instead of adding it four times.
  • One letter is 138813​ metres, so four letters use 4×138=5284×813​=852​ metres. Simplify that, then write 77 as a fraction over the same denominator so you can subtract cleanly.
Show the full solution
One letter uses 158=138185​=813​ metres, so four letters use 4×138=528=132=6124×813​=852​=213​=621​ metres. Write the roll as 7=1427=214​ and subtract. 142−132=12 metre214​−213​=21​​ metre Half a metre is well short of the 158185​ another letter would need, so no fifth letter fits.

Practice these ideas

Practice
An anchor leg is logged as 296629​ of a segment. Rewrite 296629​ as a mixed number in simplest form.
Show the solution
Each whole is 6666​, so ask how many 66's fit into 2929. Since 6×4=246×4=24 and 29−24=529−24=5, the quotient 44 is the whole part and the remainder 55 stays over 66. That gives 456465​​, already in simplest form since 55 and 66 share no factor.
Practice
A staircase rises 625652​ full turns. Rewrite 625652​ as a single improper fraction in fifths.
Show the solution
Each full turn is 5555​, so 6 turns hold 6×5=306×5=30 fifths, and the extra 2552​ brings the total to 3232 fifths. So 625=325652​=532​​. That is the whole×bottom+topwhole×bottom+top shortcut, with the denominator left alone.
Practice
A runner covers 387738​ laps. 387738​ falls between two consecutive whole numbers. What is the smaller of those two whole numbers?
Show the solution
Since 7×5=357×5=35 and 7×6=427×6=42, five whole sevens fit inside 3838 with 33 left over, so 387=537738​=573​. That sits between 55 and 66, and the smaller of those is 55​. The runner has finished 5 full laps and is partway through her sixth.
Practice
A diver's tag reads −325−352​ m: the minus covers the whole amount, so this is −3−25−3−52​. Rewrite −325−352​ as a single improper fraction.
Show the solution
Convert the positive part first. 325=3×5+25=175352​=53×5+2​=517​, and the minus covers the whole amount, so −325=−175−352​=−517​​. Since 175517​ sits between 33 and 44, the negative sits between −4−4 and −3−3, about −3.4−3.4 metres, which fits a depth reading.
Practice
A flag is planted at 234423​ on a number line. What is the largest whole number to the left of the flag?
Show the solution
23÷4=523÷4=5 with a remainder of 33, so 234=534423​=543​. The flag lands three quarters past 55, so the largest whole number to its left is 55​.
Practice
A runner starts at a trail marker 345354​ km from start, then jogs 235253​ km more. How far from start is the runner? Give as a mixed number in simplest form.
Show the solution
The wholes give 3+2=53+2=5 and the fifths give 45+35=7554​+53​=57​. Seven fifths is more than one whole, so trade it, 75=12557​=152​, and carry that whole across. The wholes become 66 with 2552​ left, so the runner is 625652​​ kilometers from the start. Improper fractions agree, 195+135=325519​+513​=532​.
Practice
Evaluate 613−223631​−232​ and write the result as a mixed number. The thirds will not subtract cleanly, so you will need to borrow one whole from the 66. What is the value?
Show the solution
1331​ is smaller than 2332​, so borrow. Take one whole from the 66, leaving 55, and turn it into 3333​, which makes 613=543631​=534​. Now the wholes give 5−2=35−2=3 and the thirds give 43−23=2334​−32​=32​, so the value is 323332​​. Improper fractions check out, 193−83=113319​−38​=311​.
Practice
Two legs: 112121​ miles and 214241​ miles. Line up fraction parts over the lcd before adding. What is the total distance as a mixed number?
Show the solution
Give both fraction parts the same bottom, 12=2421​=42​. The wholes give 1+2=31+2=3 and the fourths give 24+14=3442​+41​=43​, which is under one whole, so nothing carries. The total is 334343​​ miles, or 154415​ as an improper fraction.
Practice
Six planters each need 123132​ bags of mulch. Convert to an improper fraction, then multiply by 66. How many bags total?
Show the solution
One whole is 3333​, so 123=33+23=53132​=33​+32​=35​. Then 6×53=303=106×35​=330​=10, so the row of planters needs 1010​ bags of mulch. The improper fraction is the shortcut here, since the 66 and the 33 cancel instead of you adding 123132​ six separate times.
Practice
One press pass uses 223232​ oz of ink, and a proof run needs 3443​ of a pass. Convert, then multiply. How many ounces does the proof run use?
Show the solution
The whole number 2 is 6336​, so 223=83232​=38​ and the problem is 34×83=241243​×38​=1224​. Since 24÷12=224÷12=2, the proof run uses 22​ ounces of ink.
Practice
A ribbon is 334343​ m. Cut into 112121​ m pieces. Convert both to improper fractions, divide, write the result as a mixed number. How many pieces fit?
Show the solution
334=154343​=415​ and 112=32121​=23​, so flip the second one and multiply. 154÷32=154×23=3012=52415​÷23​=415​×32​=1230​=25​ Two goes into five twice with one left over, so 212221​​ pieces fit. Two full pieces use 33 meters and the leftover 3443​ meter is exactly half of another piece.
Practice
One loop lap is 423432​ km, and two runners split it equally. How long is each leg? Give as a mixed number in km.
Show the solution
Three thirds make one whole, so four wholes hold twelve thirds and 423=143432​=314​. Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by 1221​, so 143⋅12=146=73314​⋅21​=614​=37​, and three goes into seven twice with one left over. Each leg is 213 km231​ km​. Two legs of 213231​ add back to 423432​, the whole lap.
Practice
A full batch needs 214241​ cups of flour. You make 1331​ of a batch. How many cups do you need? Give as a fraction in simplest form.
Show the solution
A third of a batch means 13×21431​×241​, and the word "of" is the signal to multiply. Convert first, 214=84+14=94241​=48​+41​=49​, then multiply straight across. 13×94=912=3431​×49​=129​=43​​ Three quarters of a cup fits the story, since a third of a batch should use well under the full 214241​ cups.
Practice
A board is 512521​ ft. Two side brackets, each 134143​ ft, are cut off. How many feet of board remain?
Show the solution
Each bracket is 134=74143​=47​ feet, so the two together use 2×74=144=72=3122×47​=414​=27​=321​ feet. Subtracting from the board, 512−312521​−321​, the halves cancel and 5−3=25−3=2, so 22​ feet of board remain.
